q: Which host-switching genetic determinants (adhesins, capsular loci, iron-acquisition, quorum-signaling variants) actually drive E. faecalis co-infection with Streptococcus agalactiae/iniae in warm-water aquaculture, given that Akter 2023 shows a conserved fsr/ace/ebp/srtA core and a differential agg/prgB signal (BFFF11+, BFF1B1-, BFPS6-) rather than a single fish-adaptation locus?
basis: REPORT.md §4.3 documents (i) fsr/ace/ebpA/ebpC/srtA/srtC/tpx conserved in all three fish-clinical isolates and (ii) agg/prgB present only in tilapia isolate BFFF11 and absent in BFF1B1 and BFPS6 — leaving the host-switching mechanism underdetermined at the marker level. Only 13 V583-anchored VF markers were tested (§4.3, §Limitations), and cyl was uniformly absent/inconsistent, so the divergence-vs-adaptation question is genuinely open.
next_steps: Pan-genome analysis (Roary/PPanGGOLiN) across a matched cohort of ≥50 fish-clinical vs ≥50 human-clinical E. faecalis (BV-BRC + ENA), stratified by fish host species and water temperature; screen for host-associated accessory-gene enrichment; correlate with published S. iniae/S. agalactiae co-isolation reports; where isolates are available, run in-vitro tilapia-cell-line adhesion assays on agg/prgB+ vs agg/prgB- pairs.

q: How divergent is the virulence-gene repertoire (esp, gelE, asa1, cyl, ace, ebp) between fish-clinical and human-clinical E. faecalis when scored with allele-aware detection rather than fixed-threshold homology, given that our V583-anchored tblastn at pident≥80 may have under-called divergent fish-adapted alleles?
basis: REPORT.md §GENUINE CRITIQUE (ascertainment/selection bias) and §Limitations flag that the 13-marker panel was pulled from the V583 human clinical reference, so cylLS/cylLL absences and any borderline hits in fish isolates cannot be distinguished from allele-divergence-below-threshold. The paper's aggregate 69-VF count was also not reproduced (§4.3, §5) precisely because our stricter framework is DB-scoped.
next_steps: Rerun on the same three genomes with VFDB VFanalyzer (as the paper used) plus an allele-aware caller (e.g., ARIBA against a fish-Enterococcus-augmented VF reference, or pyMLST-style variant calling); cross-check with a nucleotide tblastx at relaxed thresholds; then extend to a fish-vs-human matched panel and compute per-gene dN/dS and allele-cluster diversity.

q: Is there measurable one-health transfer of AMR plasmids from aquaculture-derived E. faecalis to the human gut microbiome via the seafood chain, given that BFPS6 carries a co-located tet(L)+tet(M) tandem cassette on a single ~26.5–30 kb contig (NZ_JADBGH010000009.1) but its plasmid/replicon context was not resolved here?
basis: REPORT.md §4.2 confirms the BFPS6-exclusive tet(L)+tet(M) cassette at 100% identity co-located on one contig — a physically real MGE-candidate — but §4.6/§Limitations note PlasmidFinder was not rerun and BFPS6 is a 45-contig draft, so plasmid vs chromosomal integration, replicon type, and transferability are unresolved.
next_steps: Long-read (ONT/PacBio) resequencing of BFPS6 to close the tet cassette contig and assign plasmid replicon (rep family); MOB-suite/oriTfinder to score conjugative potential; in-vitro filter-mating from BFPS6 to a rifampicin-marked human commensal E. faecalis / E. faecium recipient; complement with a metagenomic survey of retail seafood + matched consumer-stool cohorts screening for identical tet(L)+tet(M) synteny.

q: How well are candidate vaccine-target antigens (ace collagen adhesin, ebpA/C pilus subunits, srtA/C sortases, fsrB QS receptor) conserved in sequence and in surface-epitope structure across the full genomic diversity of fish-pathogenic E. faecalis beyond the three-strain snapshot in Akter 2023?
basis: REPORT.md §4.3 shows ace/ebpA/ebpC/srtA/srtC/tpx present at 90–100% pident in all three fish isolates against the V583 reference, suggesting conservation — but the sample is n=3 strains from two Bangladeshi fish species (tilapia + sarpunti), and no epitope-level analysis or cross-strain surface-exposure modeling was performed.
next_steps: Assemble a broad fish-pathogenic E. faecalis panel (BV-BRC + NCBI + fish-disease repositories); extract ace/ebpA/ebpC/srtA/fsrB alleles; run MAFFT + entropy scoring per residue; combine with AlphaFold3/ESM-3 structural predictions and epitope-conservation mapping (BepiPred/DiscoTope); flag high-conservation surface patches as prioritized vaccine subunit candidates; validate top candidates in a tilapia challenge model.

q: Does warm-water aquaculture exert measurably stronger selection for genomic plasticity (mobile-element load, plasmid burden, prophage content, IS-element expansion) in E. faecalis than cold-water aquaculture, and does that plasticity track with AMR-cassette acquisition of the kind seen in BFPS6?
basis: REPORT.md §1 documents all three isolates as warm-water tropical (Nile tilapia, Thai sarpunti); §4.2 documents a warm-water isolate carrying a mobile tet(L)+tet(M) cassette while the two tilapia isolates carry only intrinsic lsa(A); §4.6/§Limitations note PHASTER prophage, ISfinder IS-element, and PlasmidFinder replicon claims were NOT rerun — so temperature-stratified plasticity comparisons are genuinely open.
next_steps: Assemble matched E. faecalis panels from warm-water (tropical/subtropical) vs cold-water (salmonid/trout) aquaculture with metadata (source species, water temperature range, antibiotic-use policy); rerun antiSMASH + PHASTER + ISfinder + PlasmidFinder uniformly; compare mean prophage count, IS density, plasmid-replicon count, and tet/erm/aac cassette prevalence; test with mixed-effects models controlling for host species and geography; correlate with reported farm-level antibiotic usage.
